descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-94513 AC 7, AC 12 · “Every patient access is logged and attributable to the specific signed-in physician”. Mixed: stated part — One attributed row per action class (view, save, generate, handoff send) at the server, and a handoff recipient's open as a patient access; our part — Direct API reads that bypass the client logging, and a failed logChartAccess call (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Approach · OAT-01 Signing In & Session Security · S15 Audit rows at the server: one per action class, and patient reads that leave no row (direct reads, a handoff recipient, a failed log call)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U5 Every patient access is recorded in the audit log and attributed to the signed-in physician. Each row has the patient, the physician, a timestamp and the action (view / save / generate / handoff send … (UAT OAT-01 step 5; UAT OAT-01 Expected; TFA-94513 AC 7; TFA-94513 AC 12; UAT 3.3) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given API clients for two fresh @roundai.test physicians on the local stack, each with one Hospital patient and one Nursing Home resident; the model call intercepted so no live AI call is made (e2e/support/action-observer.ts)

When (a) In Hospital and in Nursing Home: call the pre-round save, the note-generate action and handoffs send (to the second physician) directly. (b) Call rounding.get and snf.get for the caller's own patient without calling logChartAccess. (c) The recipient opens the handoff detail. …

Then (a) One row per action matching S14's predicates, each with patient_id, actor_id, _creationTime and an action/op that tells view, save, generate and handoff send apart. (b) A PHI_READ row with patient_id and actor_id for each read. (c) One row per patient in the handoff, with actor_id = the recipient. …

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): U5 per cell, with Q6 for the mapping of stored fields to actions and Q14 for which reads count. Expected today: (a) generate and handoff send fail as 'known: TFA-94513 AC 7/12'; (b) fails, because convex/access.ts states that a direct rounding.get with a valid session leaves no row; …

Handoff send: one row per send (resource handoffs, op 'send', count 1) with NO patient_id in either mode - known: TFA-94513 AC 7/12 (one row per patient vs a count is Q6). Generate: BLOCKED, not run (needs generate; forbidden on the local stack). (b) rounding.get / snf.get by the owner with a valid session leave no PHI_READ row (Q14). (c) the recipient B opened the inbox and both handoffs IN THE APP (own browser); the rows the app wrote are a PHI_READ 'handoffs.inbox' and a PHI_READ 'handoffs.detail' panel row per open and a PHI_WRITE 'read_receipt' per handoff, none naming a patient (Q14). (d) with the chart's logChartAccess call failed by the socket proxy (1 call seen and failed), the chart stays on screen with its name and pre-round text plus the alert 'Chart access couldn't be recorded. Check your connection and reload.'; the call is not retried and no PHI_READ row exists (Q14). Control through the same proxy with nothing failed: exactly one PHI_READ row (asserted).

Record only (recordOnly): (b), (c), (d) wait for Q14; (a) handoff row is known TFA-94513 AC 7/12; (a) generate blocked (needs generate).

Blocked part (blocked): (a) generate: needs generate (forbidden on the local stack)
